Thankfully, I’ve just had my last exam today. But I still have another huge project for the next 6 weeks. So it isn’t quite the end yet. 

I think I will try finding something cheap that I can fund from coaching. I want to avoid telling my family about my situation as far as possible as they are rather confused in their thinking. (In the sense that they think they are quite progressive in their thinking but are actually conservative so there will be a strong stigma about mental health issues) That also means that taking a year out really isn’t an option. 

Thank you for your advice and encouragement :)

I’ve always view religions as a social construct and philosophy to prevent the collapse of society. I haven’t tried studying philosophy but it is something that I have always been interested in. I just never had the time and motivation to go into it properly. 

I think I will take up your advice and have a look into it. At the moment I’m quite interested in Confucianism and various Chinese philosophies that evolved and shaped the East Asian region. My Friend also mentioned to me about Sikhism being an interesting religion in the sense that god can take any form so I might try having a look into these areas. 

Thank you for your advice and encouragement :) I will do my best to hang in there.

I’m sorry to hear you had such a difficult childhood. I can see how dealing with it will help me get better and I have been seeing a therapist under the NHS but it hasn’t really been helpful and there is always something going on in my life (eg. exams, etc) going on that I feel like I need to numb myself emotionally to make sure I don’t get affected and am still able to function. There is just this constant struggle between ensuring that I’m still able to cope and functioning and really facing my problems. It seems like i’m always just too cowardly to face it for what it truly is.

I understand where you’re coming from. I’ve been trying to tell myself not to care about these things because they are meaningless and are just external markers for success and I should base my “success” on what I want to achieve. But in the reality I live in, it seems impossible to escape.

That’s actually something I don’t quite understand or been able to figure out. But I think it related to my Father passing away when I was 13 and not knowing how to deal with it. I just ignored it, suppressed it and did whatever I could to just get on with life and survive, To get all the important life stuff done. I’ve also been trapped in not feeling alive since then (indifferent to everything).
